LAW 219 ROLLBACK COHERENCE — ANALYSED, PARTIALLY REPORTABLE. rollback.yml exists (175 lines) and is structurally coherent: workflow_dispatch with environment/scope/reason inputs, per-scope steps, concurrency group (rollback.yml:30-32), post-rollback health verification (:105-126), critical-path verification (:151-165), and a final always() result gate (:167-175). But three defects mean it cannot actually roll back, and none is covered by any packet record: (a) rollback.yml:69 computes LAST_COMMIT=$(git rev-parse HEAD~1) and :70 echoes it, but the script NEVER CHECKS OUT that commit — `git checkout` appears 0 times in the file, and `railway up --detach` at :73 therefore redeploys HEAD, i.e. the same commit. The rollback is a no-op on code. (b) alembic is invoked bare at :72 and :74, so it hits the same missing-script_location failure documented above. (c) The downgrade-then-redeploy-then-reupgrade sequence at :72-:74 downgrades one revision, redeploys, then runs `upgrade head` — which re-applies everything, cancelling the downgrade. So even with a correct checkout the schema would end where it started. The earlier finding that `2026_07_26_16_09`'s downgrade corrupts schema state is NOT CONFIRMED and I believe it is a misattribution: I read that file in full (41 lines) and its downgrade (:34-41) is a clean 1:1 inverse of its upgrade — 4 drop_index for 4 create_index, 3 drop_column for 3 add_column, and it contains ZERO constraint or unique-index conversions. The real asymmetry is elsewhere and is worse: 9 of 75 migrations have `def downgrade(): pass` — 2026_08_08_21_02 merge, 2026_08_21_0003/0004/0005/0006/0007, 2026_09_03_0000 merge, 2026_09_03_0001, 2026_09_04_17_00 merge — which is a direct Law 219 backward-compatibility violation. Of those, 2026_09_03_0001 is deliberate and documented (WORM audit domain, cites Law 57) and the 3 merge migrations are conventionally no-op; the 5 remaining 2026_08_21_* are undocumented.
